rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Sulami, and Ibn Abi ʿAblah read riyaah and bishran with damma on bāʾ and shīn, a plural of bashīra; this form is also reported from ʿAsim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الرياح جمعا ابن عباس والسلمي وابن أبي عبلة بشرا بضم الباء والشين ورويت عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsim also reads bishran with damma on bāʾ but sukūn on shīn, easing the pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم كذلك إلا أنه سكن الشين تخفيفا من الضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sulami, also reported from ʿAsim, reads bishran with fatḥa on bāʾ and sukūn on shīn as a verbal noun of the shortened verb bashshara.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي أيضا بشرا بفتح الباء وسكون الشين وهو مصدر بشر المخفف ورويت عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa and Ibn Qutayb read bushrā with a shortened alif, treating it as a verbal noun like رجعى.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع وابن قطيب بشرى بألف مقصورة كرجعى وهو مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight readings divide into four with nūn and four with bāʾ; their forms make bushran a circumstantial modifier of the object or, for some verbal-noun forms, potentially of the subject as well.
rows.anchor: فهذه ثماني قراءات أربعة في النون وأربع في الباء فمن قرأ بالباء جمعا أو مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending the winds means releasing or spreading them; their spreading contrasts with folding and also evokes life.
rows.anchor: لأن إرسالها هو إطلاقها وهو بمعنى النشر فكأنه قيل ينشر الرياح نشرا ووصف الريح بالنشر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains al-nashr as winds dispersed in different directions.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: في النشر إنها المتفرقة في الوجوه

rows.speaker: الشاعر (غير مسمى)
rows.claim: An unnamed poet describes the southern wind reviving the water with its breeze; the gloss says al-rayda and al-murīd mean wind.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر في وصف الريح بالإحياء والموت: وهبت له ريح الجنوب وأحييت

rows.speaker: الشاعر (غير مسمى)
rows.claim: A second unnamed poet wishes the wind would die so he can sit and rest, illustrating the wind's life and death imagery.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخر: إني لأرجو أن تموت الريح ... فأقعد اليوم وأستريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between the hands of His mercy means before His favor, namely rain, one of the greatest blessings in its effects; the human expression is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بين يدي رحمته أمام نعمته وهو المطر الذي هو من أجل النعم وأحسنها أثرا والتعيين

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani explains the present يرسل here by the preceding future-oriented دعوه خوفا وطمعا; the past أرسل in al-Furqan, Fatir, and al-Rum fits their surrounding past contexts, while al-Rum's other wording follows a future context.
rows.anchor: قال الكرماني: قال هنا يرسل لأن قبل ذلك وادعوه خوفا وطمعا فهما في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause marks the endpoint of sending the winds: they herald rain and carry clouds until those clouds are borne toward a dead land.
rows.anchor: هذه غاية لإرسال الرياح والمعنى أنه تعالى يرسل الرياح مبشرات أو مبشرات إلى سوق السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahab is a collective noun with a feminine singular form; it may be masculine or feminine and may take plural agreement.
rows.anchor: والسحاب اسم جنس بينه وبين مفرده تاء التأنيث فيذكر كقوله والسحاب المسخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine pronoun in سقناه follows the lexical form sahab, while the first-person plural magnifies God's immense favor in directing the clouds.
rows.anchor: ونسب السوق إليه تعالى بنون العظمة التفاتا لما فيه من عظيم المنة وذكر الضمير في سقناه رعيا للفظ

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi describes winds drawing clouds from the meeting of sky and earth, spreading them in the sky; heaven opens, water runs onto the clouds, and they then rain. The author says this detail is not established from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي يرسل تعالى الرياح فتأتي السحاب من بين الخافقين طرف السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: أهل الحق
rows.claim: The people of truth hold that God alone subjects and directs the winds as He wills and decrees, with no partner.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أهل الحق أن الله تعالى هو الذي يسخر الرياح ويصرفها حيث أراد بمشيئته وتقديره لا مشارك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Razi refuted the philosophers' account of how winds arise on four grounds and also refuted the astrologers' account, concluding that God is their mover by rational proof.
rows.anchor: وللفلاسفة كيفية في حصول الرياح ذكرها أبو عبد الله الرازي وأبطلها من وجوه أربعة

rows.speaker: ابن عمران
rows.claim: Ibn ʿImran classifies four winds as punishment—qāṣif, ʿāṣif, ṣarṣar, and ʿaqīm—and four as mercy—nashirāt, mubashshirāt, mursalāt, and dhāriyāt.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمران الرياح ثمان أربع منها عذاب وهي: القاصف والعاصف والصرصر والعقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the lām in li-balad as a lām of conveyance, meaning the rain is delivered to the land.
rows.anchor: واللام في لبلد عندي لام التبليغ كقولك قلت لك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the lām as causal, meaning the winds drive clouds for the sake of a land.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لأجل بلد فجعل اللام لام العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees little apparent difference between conveyance and cause: saying one drove wealth for someone entails its delivery, unlike driving it for someone's sake, which need not reach that person.
rows.anchor: ولا يظهر فرق بين قولك سقت لك مالا وسقت لأجلك مالا فإن الأول معناه أوصلته لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the land dead is a fitting metaphor for barrenness and lack of growth, like a body without life; the land is singled out as the place where people gather and settle and where mercy appears.
rows.anchor: ووصف البلد بالموت استعارة حسنة لجدبه وعدم نباته كأنه من حيث عدم الانتفاع به كالجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasin uses the general phrase dead earth because it highlights resurrection through signs of God's power, including night and the carrying of descendants.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في سورة يس المقصد إظهار الآيات العظيمة الدالة على البعث جاء التركيب باللفظ العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsim, Abu ʿAmr, and al-Aʿmash read the yāʾ in mayyit with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وسكن ياء الميت عاصم وأبو عمرو والأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-anzalna bihi al-maʾ, the bāʾ is locative and the pronoun refers to the nearest antecedent, the dead land.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الباء ظرفية والضمير عائد على بلد ميت أي فأنزلنا فيه الماء وهو أقرب مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings of the pronoun take the bāʾ as causal and refer it to the clouds, or refer it to the implied act of driving the clouds.
rows.anchor:
وقيل الباء سببية والضمير
عائد على السحاب. وقيل عائد على المصدر المفهوم من سقناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects taking the pronoun back to an implied verbal noun, since a suitable expressed antecedent is already present.
rows.anchor: والثالث ضعيف لأنه عائد على غير مذكور مع وجود المذكور وصلاحيته للعود عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal makes the bāʾ mean min and the pronoun refer to clouds, as in يشرب بها; the author says this is poor because it forces one preposition to carry another's sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عائد على السحاب والباء بمعنى من أي فأنزلنا منه الماء كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the second bihi of fa-akhrajna bihi has the same disputed antecedents; one proposal shifts the first pronoun to clouds and the second to the land without an intervening separator.
rows.anchor: فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات الخلاف في به كالخلاف السابق في به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing out fruit is a visible analogue for bringing the dead from their graves alive to the gathering, so people should recall their promised resurrection from the renewal of plants.
rows.anchor: أي مثل هذا الإخراج نخرج الموتى من قبورهم أحياء إلى الحشر لعلكم تذكرون بإخراج الثمرات

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Razin al-ʿUqayli asks the Prophet how God will restore creation and what sign is in creation; the Prophet points to a dry valley later seen green as God's sign.
rows.anchor: خرج البيهقي وغيره عن رزين العقيلي قال قلت: يا رسول الله كيف يعيد الله الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author leaves two possible scopes for the simile: the general act of bringing forth, with fruits proving God's power to raise the dead, or the same manner of resurrection through rain that revives the dead land.
rows.anchor: وهل التشبيه في مطلق الإخراج ودلالة إخراج الثمرات على القدرة في إخراج الأموات أم في كيفية الإخراج

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that life-water from beneath the Throne rains for forty years, the dead grow like crops, receive spirits, sleep, then rise at the second trumpet and hear that this is the Merciful's promise.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن أبي هريرة أنه يمطر عليهم من ماء تحت العرش يقال له ماء الحيوان أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good land is fertile, excellent soil; the bad land is saline and poor, unable to grow useful plants.
rows.anchor: الطيب الجيد الترب الكريم الأرض، والذي خبث المكان السبخ الذي لا ينبت ما ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse completes the account of fruit by describing the customary difference between growth from good soil and saline soil.
rows.anchor: ولما قال فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات تمم هذا المعنى بكيفية ما يخرج من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A description of good, full growth is omitted after يخرج نباته; context, the contrast with poor yield, and بإذن ربه make the intended sense clear.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حال محذوفة أي يخرج نباته وافيا حسنا وحذفت لفهم المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-idhni rabbihi is a circumstantial phrase meaning by God's facilitation; it praises the good land even though both kinds of growth occur by God's permission.
rows.anchor: وبإذن ربه في موضع الحال وخص خروج نبات الطيب بقوله بإذن ربه على سبيل المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both clauses omit the word land, but their different forms—adjective in the first and relative clause in the second—vary the style while preserving the contrast.
rows.anchor: وحذف من الجملة الثانية الموصوف أيضا والتقدير والبلد الذي خبث لدلالة والبلد الطيب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of لا يخرج refers to the bad land as an omitted noun; its possessive plant is understood through an omitted annexation in either clause.
rows.anchor: والفاعل في لا يخرج عائد على الذي خبث وقد قلنا إنه صفة لموصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada take the two lands as a parable for souls: the believer returns easily and well to the body, while the disbeliever returns with difficulty, as each left at death.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة مثال لروح المؤمن يرجع إلى جسده سهلا طيبا كما خرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the parable interpretation, the contrast in souls refers back to the preceding statement that God brings out the dead.
rows.anchor: فيكون هذا راجعا من حيث المعنى إلى قوله كذلك نخرج الموتى أي على هذين الوصفين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads the lands as hearts receiving the Qurʾan like rain: the believer accepts and benefits from it, while the unbeliever's barren heart gains nothing.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي مثال للقلوب لما نزل القرآن كنزول المطر على الأرض فقلب المؤمن كالأرض الطيبة

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the lands exemplify the intelligent and the dull.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: هو مثال للفهيم والبليد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the example to distinguish people affected by admonition and reminder from those untouched by them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وهذا مثل لمن ينجع فيه الوعظ والتنبيه من المكلفين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the good and bad as Adam's good and wicked descendants.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد ذرية آدم خبيث وطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors a literal account of God's customary growth from good and bad land, with no intended parable of the kinds proposed by earlier interpreters.
rows.anchor: والأظهر ما قدمناه من أن المقصود التعريف بعبادة الله تعالى في إخراج النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAblah, Abu Haywah, and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read yukhraju nabātuhu in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وأبو حيوة وعيسى بن عمر يخرج نباته مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaqaʿ reads nakdan with fatḥa on the kāf, which al-Zajjaj identifies as the Medinan reading; Ibn Musarrif reads it with sukūn, and both are verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن القعقاع نكدا بفتح الكاف، قال الزجاج: وهي قراءة أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the bad land's growth to poor yield emphatically says it cannot produce otherwise and hints that an entrenched bad nature is far from turning toward good.
rows.anchor: وكون نبات الذي خبث محصورا خروجه على حالة النكد مبالغة شديدة في كونه لا يكون إلا هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are varied and repeated proofs of God's oneness, power, and freely chosen action; rain and vegetation sustain life, making them a great blessing for which people should give thanks.
rows.anchor: أي مثل هذا التصريف والترديد والتنويع ننوع الآيات ونرددها وهي الحجج الدالة على الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Noah narrative follows the creation and afterlife themes and the command to leave those who play with religion; it consoles the initially unbelieving Prophet by recalling earlier messengers and their peoples.
rows.anchor: قص تعالى عليه أحوال الرسل الذين كانوا قبله وأحوال من بعثوا إليه على سبيل التسلية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is introduced first as a second Adam and the first messenger sent to those on earth; his people persisted most in denial and responded least.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بنوح إذ هو آدم الأصغر وأول رسول بعث إلى من في الأرض وأمته أدوم تكذيبا له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Noah was forty when sent; other reports give fifty, one hundred, two hundred fifty, three hundred, three hundred fifty, or four hundred years, a discrepancy the author calls great.
rows.anchor: وكان نجارا بعثه الله إلى قومه وهو ابن أربعين سنة قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says the flood occurred in the 1,600th year of Noah's life.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الطوفان كان سنة ألف وستمائة من عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was the first messenger after Adam to forbid marriage to daughters, sisters, aunts, and maternal aunts; all people now descend from Noah.
rows.anchor: وهو أول الرسل بعد آدم بتحريم البنات والأخوات والعمات والخالات وجميع الخلق الآن من ذرية نوح

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri assigns Arabs, Persians, Romans, Syrians, and Yemenis to Shem; Indians and several African peoples to Ham; and Turks, Berbers, peoples beyond China, Gog and Magog, and Slavs to Japheth.
rows.anchor: وعن الزهري أن العرب وفارسا والروم وأهل الشام واليمن من ذرية سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani notes that لقد أرسلنا begins without a conjunction here, unlike Hud and al-Muʾminun, because those passages already mention messengers and implicitly Noah through the Ark, which he was first to make.
rows.anchor: لقد أرسلنا استئناف كلام دون واو وفي هود والمؤمنون ولقد بواو العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لقد is the response to an unstated oath and emphasizes the report.
rows.anchor: واللام جواب قسم محذوف أكد تعالى هذا الإخبار بالقسم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says an oath clause emphasizes its answer and therefore creates the expectation associated with qad; a quoted line illustrates the rare lām without qad.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : ما لهم لا يكادون ينطقون بهذه اللام إلا مع قد

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some grammarians say an affirmative inflected past close to the present takes qad with the lām to mark nearness; without qad, the speaker does not intend that closeness.
rows.anchor: وبعض أصحابنا يقول إذا أقسم على جملة مصدرة بماض مثبت متصرف وكان قريبا من زمان الحال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses أرسلنا as بعثنا, while another interpretation says Noah was entrusted with a message to deliver, so the message itself entails his commission.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أرسلنا بعثنا وقال غيره حملناه رسالة يؤديها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's speech is introduced with fa here and in al-Muʾminun, while the Hud, Salih, and Shuʿayb accounts omit it for stylistic breadth because the semantic connection suffices.
rows.anchor: وهنا فقال بفاء العطف وكذا في المؤمنون في قصة عاد وصالح وشعيب هنا قال بغير فاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hud, إني لكم is understood as introduced by an omitted saying verb, meaning he said that he was sent to them.
rows.anchor: وفي قصة نوح في هود إني لكم على إضمار القول أي فقال إني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing them as his people draws attention, seeks their affection, and reminds them of kinship so that they should not oppose him.
rows.anchor: وفي ندائه قومه تنبيه لهم لما يلقيه إليهم واستعطاف وتذكير بأنهم قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech commands worship of God alone and rejection of their named idols; its explanation of God's unique divinity gives the reason for worship and is joined without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: ومعمول القول جملة الأمر بعبادة الله وحده ورفض آلهتهم المسماة ودا وسواعا ويغوث ويعوق ونسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, Abu Jaʿfar, and al-Kisaʾi read غيره in the genitive as an appositive or adjective to إله; the other canonical readers use the nominative, while ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar uses the accusative as an exception.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأعمش وأبو جعفر والكسائي غيره بالجر على لفظ إله بدلا أو نعتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, من إله is a subject and لكم its predicate; another analysis omits the predicate, understood as in existence, with لكم specifying it.
rows.anchor: ومن إله مبتدأ ولكم في موضع الخبر، وقيل: الخبر محذوف أي في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخاف may mean certainty, since Noah knows punishment will come if they disbelieve, or caution in the ordinary sense because they might yet believe; the great day may be Judgment or the worldly flood.
rows.anchor: وأخاف قيل: بمعنى أتيقن وأجزم لأنه عالم أن العذاب ينزل بهم إن لم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning expresses Noah's compassion and tenderness toward his people.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الجملة إظهار الشفقة والحنو عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah does not merely deny being in obvious error; he denies even one trace of misguidance touching him, a stronger rebuttal than simply saying he is not misguided.
rows.anchor: لم يرد النفي منه على لفظ ما قالوه فلم يأت التركيب لست في ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His second address, despite their rudeness, shows a broad heart and gentle treatment.
rows.anchor: وفي ندائه لهم ثانيا والإعراض عن جفائهم ما يدل على سعة صدره والتلطف بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having denied misguidance, Noah says he is a messenger, the opposite state, and that his Lord is also theirs because they belong to the worlds He owns and cares for.
rows.anchor: ولما نفى عنهم التباس ضلالة ما به دل على أنه على الصراط المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبلغكم may stand as an explanatory independent sentence or as an adjective of رسول; its wording can track the first-person speaker or the noun messenger.
rows.anchor: وأبلغكم استئناف على سبيل البيان بكونه رسولا أو جملة في موضع الصفة لرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads أبلغكم without doubling the lām here, at both locations in this sūra and in al-Ahqaf; the other canonical readers use the causative doubled form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو أبلغكم هنا في الموضعين وفي الأحقاف بالتخفيف وباقي السبعة بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural رسالات may refer to revelations over a long period, different kinds of instruction, warning, exhortation, and good news, or revelations given to Noah and earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: وجمع رسالات باعتبار ما أوحي إليه في الأزمان المتطاولة أو باعتبار المعاني المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report locates those earlier revelations in thirty pages of Idris and fifty pages of Shith.
rows.anchor: قيل: في صحف إدريس وهي ثلاثون صحيفة وفي صحف شيث وهي خمسون صحيفة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the lām in أنصح لكم emphasizes that advice is sincerely intended for the recipient, though a counselor may also seek personal benefit.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وفي زيادة اللام مبالغة ودلالة على إمحاض النصيحة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari adds that no advice is more beneficial than God's and His messengers' advice.
rows.anchor: فرب نصيحة ينتفع بها الناصح بقصد النفعين جميعا ولا نصيحة أنفع من نصيحة الله تعالى ورسله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Arabic normally says نصحت لك rather than نصحتك.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: لا تكاد العرب تقول نصحتك إنما نصحت لك

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's line نصحت بني عوف فلم يتقبلوا is cited in the discussion of whether advice takes a direct object or the lām construction.
rows.anchor: نصحت بني عوف فلم يتقبلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vague phrase what you do not know conveys threat by presenting unknown divine power and punishment as things they ought to fear; it may also mean matters revealed to Noah.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله ما لا تعلمون إبهام عليهم وهو عام ولكن ساق ذلك مساق المعلومات التي يخاف عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says every prophet sent to people had a miracle, though some miracles are known to us and others are not.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولا بد أن نوحا عليه السلام وكل نبي مبعوث إلى الخلق كانت له معجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence maps Noah's mission: first he delivers God's messages, then sincerely guides them toward safety through exclusive worship, and finally warns of God's vengeance if they refuse.
rows.anchor: قال أولا أبلغكم رسالات ربي وهذا مبدأ أمره معهم وهو التبليغ، كما قال:

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains that Noah's people considered it astonishing both that a warning came to them and that God sent a human messenger to demand worship of Him alone and abandonment of their idols.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي سبب استبعادهم إرسال نوح والهمزة للإنكار والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes their surprise: God has complete authority to send whomever He wills to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: أي هذا مما لا يعجب منه إذ له تعالى، التصرف التام بإرسال من يشاء لمن يشاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes the waw as coordinating an omitted charge, effectively asking whether they denied and wondered that the reminder came.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: الواو للعطف والمعطوف محذوف كأنه قيل أو كذبتم وعجبتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects an omitted coordinated clause as contrary to Sibawayh and the grammarians: waw coordinates with what precedes, while the interrogative hamza moves before the conjunction.
rows.anchor: وهو كلام مخالف لكلام سيبويه والنحاة لأنهم يقولون: إن الواو لعطف ما بعدها على ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikr may mean admonition, revelation, a miracle, a miraculous book, or clarification; the author favors the sense of warning about what is feared.
rows.anchor: والذكر الوعظ أو الوحي أو المعجز أو كتاب معجز أو البيان أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On على رجل, possible analyses supply على لسان, take على as meaning مع, or keep the preposition literal with جاءكم meaning descended to you; the people objected to a human prophet rather than an angel.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يكون قوله على رجل فيه إضمار أي على لسان رجل كما قال ما وعدتنا على رسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder comes to warn of the feared outcome, warning aims at their piety, and piety is ordered toward mercy; the chain of consequences lets the arrival be explained by all of them.
rows.anchor: والإنذار بالمخوف لأجل وجود التقوى منهم ووجود التقوى لرجاء الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite Noah's gentle appeal and compassion, his people denied what he brought from God, so God saved Noah and those who believed and drowned the deniers.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى أنهم كذبوه هذا مع حسن ملاطفته لهم ومراجعته لهم وشفقته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers aboard the Ark are variously said to be forty men, eighty men and forty women according to al-Kalbi, or ten people including Noah's three sons; another count says nine including his three sons.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أربعين رجلا، وقيل ثمانين رجلا وأربعين امرأة قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A village near Mosul is said to be named for the eighty people saved with Noah.
rows.anchor: وإليهم تنسب القرية التي ينسب إليها الثمانون وهي بالموصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of those who denied God's signs identifies denial as the cause of drowning and implies that Noah had signs proving his mission.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا إعلام بعلة الغرق وهو التكذيب وبآياتنا يقتضي أن نوحا كانت له آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Ark may attach to the relative clause, describing those settled aboard, or to saved them, meaning they were rescued from the flood in the ship; there it may also mean because of the ship.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق في الفلك بما يتعلق به الظرف الواقع صلة أي والذين استقروا معه في الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿamīn describes people blind in heart and lacking insight; its form presents blindness as an established trait.
rows.anchor: وعمين من عمي القلب أي غير مستبصرين ويدل على ثبوت هذا الوصف كونه جاء على وزن فعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says their hearts were blind to recognizing God's oneness, prophethood, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس عميت قلوبهم عن معرفة التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: معاذ النحوي
rows.claim: Muʿadh al-Nahwi distinguishes ʿam as blindness in one's affairs from aʿmā for physical blindness, while noting forms may overlap.
rows.anchor: وقال معاذ النحوي: رجل عم في أمره لا يبصره وأعمى في البصر

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth glosses a man described as ʿam as blind of heart.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: رجل عم إذا كان أعمى القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAd is the name of a people and is therefore declined; some treat it as the name of a tribe and leave it indeclinable.
rows.anchor: عاد اسم الحي ولذلك صرفه وبعضهم جعله اسما للقبيلة فمنعه الصرف

rows.speaker: الشاعر (غير مسمى)
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line about ʿAd in the time of ʿAd is cited as evidence in the discussion of the name's grammatical form.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لو شهدت عاد في زمان عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lineage given for the people is ʿAd son of ʿAws son of Iram son of Shem son of Noah.
rows.anchor: سميت القبيلة باسم أبيهم وهو عاد بن عوص بن إرم بن سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأبدي
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi says the known view is that Hud was an Arab; Sibawayh's grouping of him with Noah and Lot appears to imply that he considered Hud foreign.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا أبو الحسن الأبدي النحوي: المعروف أن هودا عربي والذي يظهر من كلام سيبويه

rows.speaker: أبو البركات الجواني
rows.claim: Abu al-Barakat al-Juwani reports Yemen's claim that Yaʿrub son of Qahtan son of Hud first spoke Arabic and settled Yemen, making Hud non-Arab; he gives Hud's line through ʿAbir, Shalakh, Arfakhshadh, and Shem to Noah.
rows.anchor: وذكر الشريف النسابة أبو البركات الجواني أن يعرب بن قحطان بن هود هو الذي زعمت يمن

rows.speaker: أبو البركات الجواني
rows.claim: A second genealogy makes Hud son of ʿAbd Allah son of Riyah son of al-Jalud son of ʿAd, hence one of the people of ʿAd; his mother was Marjana, and he was a merchant said to resemble Adam most.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من عاد وهو هود بن عبد الله بن رياح بن الجلود بن عاد بن عوص
